summary.text: Collin Corbett, an independent political strategist and small-business owner, lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Illinois to JB Pritzker.
He ran as an independent after a career as a Republican campaign strategist.

paragraphs.text: Corbett lives in Palatine and founded Cor Strategies, EmpowerPolitics and Long9 Studio.
He says he has recruited and trained over 3,500 people to participate in politics.
Cor Strategies has helped Republican candidates run for office.

Corbett left Cor Strategies after the primary, saying he was concerned that the Republican Party supports violent immigration raids and no longer welcomes opposing opinions, and he ended his "Smoke-Filled Room" podcast.
He filed about 37,000 signatures to run for governor as an independent on May 26, 2026.
His running mate was Carolyn Schofield of Crystal Lake, a former Republican McHenry County Board member.
Corbett said he wanted to bring a more balanced voice to a race between Gov. JB Pritzker and Republican nominee Darren Bailey.
His platform called for property, sales and income tax changes and for making fixes at DCFS a top priority.
During the campaign, his platform emphasized affordability, including tax changes, and fixing the Department of Children and Family Services.
He received 3.4% of the vote to JB Pritzker's 60.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Former Republican strategist Collin Corbett files to run for governor as independent
